name: Lake Kol-Ukok
near: The village of Isakeev (start of the transfer/trail, CBT Kochkor, TUK); Kochkor is the organisation’s base, about 20 km of dirt road to the start of the trail (Beyond Wild Places).
elev: About 3,050 m at the lake (TUK, Kyrgyzstan-tourism); trail start ~2,600 m (TUK); the highest point of the hiking approach is 3,166 m (Beyond Wild Places).
short: A mountain lake at about 3,000 m in the Terskey Ala-Too range south of Kochkor: 4.5 hours on foot (14.5 km) or on horseback, summer yurt camps and a side trip to Lake Kol-Tor.
desc: Kol-Ukok (“chest lake”) is a high-mountain lake at about 3,050 m in the north-eastern part of the Terskey Ala-Too range south of Kochkor, up to 17 m deep (Kyrgyzstan-tourism). Sevan trout, brought from Armenia, live in the lake (Eurasia Travel). All around is the herders’ summer jailoo (summer pasture); in summer three small yurt camps operate on the shore (including Cholponai). Approach: a transfer from Kochkor to the village of Isakeev/the start of the trail (~2,600 m), then 14.5 km on foot with a climb of about 1,100 m (4.5 h) or on horseback through the Ters-Tor valley. A popular side trip from the lake goes to the higher Lake Kol-Tor (10–12 km round trip, up to ~3,400–3,489 m) — not to be confused with the Kol-Tor in the Kegety gorge. Multi-day horse routes over the Ukok Pass (3,871 m) into the Tuura-Suu valley also start from here.
guide: Leave Kochkor early: a taxi to the start of the trail costs about 600 som, then it is 4.5 hours up the valley — the 1,100 m gain is noticeable, but the trail is clear. Spend the night at the lake: at Cholponai camp a yurt with dinner and breakfast costs about 2,100 som. In the morning go light to Kol-Tor (5–6 h round trip) — it is the best view of the hike. There is no phone coverage at the lake, but you can get a signal on the road above the camps — warn your family in advance. If you do not want to walk, CBT Kochkor can arrange a horse from Isakeev.
see: The lake itself in its mountain bowl; yurts and herds on the jailoo; the Ters-Tor valley on the approach; as a side trip — Lake Kol-Tor (up to 3,489 m) with views of the range; panoramas of the Kochkor valley on the way down. For anglers — Sevan trout in the lake (Eurasia Travel); for a multi-day trip — the Ukok Pass (3,871 m) and the Tuura-Suu valley.
skip: You are not ready for a 4.5 h climb (+1,100 m) and do not want to ride — you cannot drive to the lake. You are already going to Song-Kol or Kol-Suu and are short of time. You tolerate altitude above 3,000 m badly.
diff: Moderate: 14.5 km one way, ~1,100 m gain, ~4.5 h (Beyond Wild Places); TUK rates its two-day route (24 km, ~450 m gain per day) as moderate. The side trip to Kol-Tor: 12 km, +520 m, 5.5 h.
when: June to August (TUK departures); Kyrgyzstan-tourism runs tours from May to August (hiking) and from June to September (horse). Plan the trip for dry weather: rain washes out the dirt road from Kochkor (Eurasia Travel). In winter and spring there is snow on the trail.
hours: An open natural area with no ticket office. The yurt camps operate only in summer (June to August/early September; check the exact dates of Cholponai camp on Google Maps/Instagram).
daytime: Start on the trail in the morning (7–9 h) to arrive by noon and avoid afternoon thunderstorms; evening and dawn at the lake have the best light; go to Kol-Tor in the morning.
how: Bishkek → Kochkor (200 km, ~3 h; marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek bus station). Kochkor → start of the trail at Isakeev: ~20 km of dirt road, about 1 h (4×4 or taxi). Then 14.5 km on foot (4.5 h) up through the Ters-Tor valley, or on horseback.
needcar: Yes, to the start of the trail: a taxi/car from Kochkor (~600 som per car, can be shared), a CBT Kochkor or TUK transfer. The approach to the lake itself is on foot or by horse; there is no road to the lake.
self: Yes: the trail is obvious, no permits or fees; you need an offline map/track, a tent or a yurt booking. A taxi to the trail can be found in Kochkor.
roadtype: Paved road Bishkek — Kochkor; from Kochkor ~20 km of dirt road to Isakeev/the start (4×4 preferable); then only a foot/horse mountain trail through Ters-Tor — not a road for cars. After rain the dirt road washes out and becomes hard to pass (Eurasia Travel).
traveltime: Bishkek — Kochkor ~3 h; Kochkor — trail start ~1 h; the climb to the lake 4.5 h (14.5 km); to Kol-Tor and back 5.5 h. The TUK programme: 2 days, 24 km in total.
stay: Three small yurt camps by the lake; Yurt Camp Cholponai — 2,100 som per person per night with dinner and breakfast (Beyond Wild Places; contact via Google Maps/Instagram). Tents — free camping by the lake (in the TUK programme tents, the yurt and dinner cost extra). In Kochkor — CBT Kochkor guesthouses. Kyrgyzstan-tourism uses a family yurt camp (up to 4 people per yurt, B&B).
net: No phone coverage at the lake; a signal can be caught on the road above the yurt camps (Beyond Wild Places). The operator is not stated; in Kochkor — Beeline/O!/MegaCom.
entry: Free: no source (TUK, CBT Kochkor, Beyond Wild Places) reports any entry fee or eco fee.
transfer: Taxi Kochkor — trail start ~600 som per car (Beyond Wild Places); Bishkek — Kochkor marshrutka 350 som (May 2026); a 2-day TUK tour 5,000 som per person with transport. A ready-made 2-day tour from Bishkek by 4×4 with a yurt and guide — $150–390 per person depending on group size (Kyrgyzstan-tourism).
bring: Trekking footwear, a tent and a warm sleeping bag (nights at 3,000 m are cold), a rain jacket, sun protection, water and a snack for the 4.5 h climb, cash for the yurt, an offline map, a power bank, a water purifier.
warn: Altitude ~3,000–3,500 m (with Kol-Tor) — altitude sickness is possible; weather changes quickly, thunderstorms after noon. No phone coverage at the lake. Do not confuse the Kol-Tor above Kol-Ukok with Lake Kol-Tor in the Kegety gorge (Chuy region). Herders’ dogs near the camps.
food: Dinner and breakfast in the yurt camp (included in the 2,100 som at Cholponai): national dishes, tea, bread; in summer the herders have kumys. A local feature is the Sevan trout from the lake (Eurasia Travel); whether the camps serve it is not confirmed.
reviews: Google Maps (“Kelukek”): 4.9/5, 48 ratings (03.10.2026). Blogs (Beyond Wild Places): pros — an accessible overnight hike from Kochkor, a beautiful lake, a side trip to Kol-Tor; cons — a noticeable altitude gain, no phone coverage at the lake, simple yurts.
photos.0.cap: A yurt camp on the approach to Kol-Ukok; not a view of the lake itself
p.sum: Kol-Ukok (~3,050 m) is the easiest high-mountain hike from Kochkor: marshrutka No. 513 Bishkek — Kochkor (300–350 som), a taxi to the bridge at the edge of the village/start of the dirt road (≈600 som per car, saves ~7 km), then 14.5 km along a dirt road with a climb of ≈1,100 m (≈4.5 h) through the Ters-Tor valley. At the lake there are three small yurt camps (Cholponai — 2,100 som per person with dinner and breakfast, 2025) and free camping; on the second day — a side trip to Lake Kol-Tor (12 km, 5.5 h). No phone coverage at the lake; after rain the dirt road from Kochkor turns to mud.

p.season: May: snow on the upper sections. June — August: main season (TUK, yurts). September: quiet, cold at night, horse tours until the end of the month. October — April: snow. After rain in any month — mud on the dirt road.
p.budget.economy: ≈3,500–4,000 som per person for 2 days: marshrutka 2×300–350, share of a taxi 150–300, yurt with meals 2,100 (or a tent for free); or a TUK hike 5,000 som.
p.budget.comfort: Tour from Bishkek $150–390 per person; private horse tour from Kochkor $650 per group.
p.permits: TUK, CBT Kochkor and Beyond Wild Places mention no permits or fees on site; Eurasia Travel writes about a “special permit” — not confirmed by other sources.
p.access: Teenagers and active children — yes (14.5 km and +1,100 m); small children — on horseback with a guide. Older people — only on horseback/with a horse tour. Strollers — no. Dogs are allowed; herders’ dogs at the yurts.
